headline: Reach the server inside a Tailscale or WireGuard tunnel
summary: Sync clients that reach the HermitStash server over a Tailscale/WireGuard tunnel can now verify it by a pinned server key instead of the tunnel hostname, which the server's external TLS certificate does not carry.

items.title: Tunnel mode
items.body: When the server is reached inside a Tailscale (or other WireGuard) tunnel — on its MagicDNS name or tailnet IP — its external TLS leaf will not carry that hostname, so the normal hostname/SAN check fails. Tunnel mode skips only that hostname match while still enforcing the pinned server SPKI, the mTLS chain, and the post-quantum group floor; the tunnel, the pin, and mTLS bind the server's identity. Enable it at enrollment with "hermitstash-sync init --tunnel" (or HERMITSTASH_TUNNEL_MODE=1 for a headless setup), which captures and pins the server's leaf key over the first-contact connection and turns tunnel mode on. It is explicit opt-in only — never inferred from a URL — and fail-closed: turning it on without a pinned server key is refused, because relaxing the hostname check with no pin would accept any chain-valid certificate.
